p: Every step reaches the same states whatever its type: enqueued, executing, resolved. A step that throws adds an attempt and a backoff and goes round again.

p: A discovery request is the SDK reporting what to run next. When one reports more than one step, it gets its own bar and a ribbon down to the steps it reported.

figure.figcaption: Blue is the discovery request. The ribbon threads the steps it reported. Cables appear on hover or select and point at what caused the row.

div: A discovery bar appears only where the request reported more than one step. A request that reported one step, which is the next step in a chain or the step after a coalesce, is a single execution and rolls into that step’s row.
p: Today the Run row is a full width bar in the run’s status colour. The header, the status badge and the axis already report that. It could instead report where the elapsed time went.

svg.aria-label: The run row today compared with a compute profile
svg.text: today: the run’s status, full width, repeating the axis
as an execution profile: grey is elapsed, colour is SDK execution

figure.figcaption: Grey is elapsed time with no SDK execution. Colour is time the SDK was executing, discovery requests and finalization included. Any failure in a slice colours it red — a cluster of failures among successes is the thing an overview exists to show.

p: A run can be nine days elapsed and five seconds executing. Dead time is worth almost none of the width, and the threshold is low: anything with nothing executing for more than a few percent of the run collapses to a band, and an hour and a week get the same few pixels.

figure.figcaption: The cut takes the middle of the sleep, so the bar visibly begins, is torn, and resumes. The Run row’s own track tears rather than carrying a glyph laid on top of it, and what runs through the band is blurred and desaturated — it is left sharp on the Run row, because the tear is the thing saying “compressed here”.

div: Only the drawing compresses. Every reported duration is still wall clock.
p: The width left over is split between the surviving stretches in proportion to their real duration, which is the same thing as saying a second is worth the same number of pixels wherever it lands. Two spans either side of a compressed gap stay comparable, and several compressions need no special case.

svg.aria-label: the leftover width splits by real duration

figure.figcaption: Thirty seconds of work on one side and ten on the other: the remaining width splits 75/25.

p: The bands share one budget, so a run full of idle stretches does not spend its width on the parts where nothing happened. They thin instead, and below a width that can hold them a band drops its label, then its tear, leaving a marked line. The rules and the blur never go — they are what says not to scale.

figure.figcaption: Eight compressions sharing one budget. The polls between them still share the one scale.

p:
A step instrumented with @inngest/otel reports what your code did inside it — HTTP calls, database queries, third-party APIs. Everything above this point is Inngest’--s:0">chargeat rest
chargePOST /paySELECTUPDATEselected

The same at any complexity. Spans inside a Promise.all overlap, and on their own pitch that reads as exactly what it is —--s:0">fanoutat rest
fanoutGET /aGET /bGET /cSELECTUPDATEselected

A span is a plain bar on a tighter pitch: no queue mark, no start, no resolution circle. The event vocabulary belongs to the trace, and a span is something that happened inside one row of it.


chargePOST /paySELECTUPDATEExpanded: indented, thinner, same status colours. The step is still the thing that retried — a span inside it is not separately retryable.

The nesting is a claim, and the trace has to be able to keep it.

chargePOST /paySELECTA span sits inside its step, because that is where it ran. One that outruns it is a clock disagreement between your process and ours, not a slow query, and the row says so rather than clamping quietly.


The selected row

A row is plotted against the whole run, so a step that took ten seconds inside a twenty minute run is a few pixels wide and its marks overlap. Selecting it replots that row across the full width using the same bars and marks, and names each piece: intervals with their durations, marks with what happened. Hover a piece for its description.


abcin the trace
cqueued1.2sattempt 12.4sbackoff1.9squeued720msattempt 24.1squeuedstartedretryqueuedstartedokselected

This is not a second way of drawing a run. Same bars, same marks, more width.


Annotations

Optional, usually a duration. The annotation sits after the row’s last bar rather than in a fixed column, so it takes no horizontal space and disappears when there is nothing to report.

a34msb2 attempts · 20mscplanned 3rdnap 2sno computeA duration after the bar it belongs to. The same slot can carry an attempt count, a flow control reason, or the number of runs an event started.



Step typesevery step type and the states it reaches



step.run
queuedrunningsucceededretriedfailedcancelledAttempts, backoff and the result are intervals in one row, not separate rows.

step.sleep
sleepingfinishedcancelledBlue while it is running, like anything unresolved. It goes green because step.sleep() cannot fail: it elapses, or the run is cancelled.

step.waitForEvent
waitingmatchedtimed outcancelledA timeout is a result, not a failure.

step.waitForSignal
receivedcancelledSame states as step.waitForEvent(). Only what resolves it differs.

step.invoke
runningfinishedfailedcancelledThe bar is the child run’s duration, drawn on this run’s axis.

step.sendEvent
sentsent nothingfailed2 runs ↗The row reports how many runs the events started, and that count is the way into them.







Scenarios

Ordered from one step to the cases that are hard to draw. Each shows the run at rest and, where it differs, on hover or select.

User docs

The page we would ship, rendered from docs/understanding-traces.md with its figures resolved to the live drawings. If a rule changes and this stops being true, that is the signal.


Every function run produces a trace: one row per thing that happened, on one time axis. It shows what your code did, what Inngest did around it, and where the time actually went.

Two rules cover almost all of it.

The two rules

Bars are intervals. Colour says what kind of work, fill says whether your code was running.

SolidYour function was executing. This is the part you pay for.
HatchedNothing of yours was running — queued, sleeping, waiting, backing off.

Circles are moments. Hollow means unresolved, filled means resolved.

Only a resolution circle is ever green or red. Everything before it is neutral, so the outcome of a row is always the last thing on it.

That is the whole encoding. Two sequential steps, read left to right:

http · aconnect · aThe same run over HTTP and over Connect.

Two differences sit inside the spans. A Connect run carries no inngest.http.timing, so there is no network breakdown to expand. The connect proxy polls for the SDK response every 2s plus a random 0 to 3s;--s:0">connect · aproxy poll: 2s + rand(0…3s) if the push is missed
